title: Give a 1 mL intramuscular injection into a deltoid trainer with a retractable safety syringe
instruction: Give the 1 mL dose in the syringe as an intramuscular injection in the training arm's deltoid, pushing the plunger slowly and steadily. Push it all the way so the needle retracts, then put the syringe in the sharps container and the needle cap in the waste cup.
context: Giving injections is core work for medical assistants (O*NET 31-9092.00, about 0.8 million US jobs), licensed practical nurses (29-2061.00, 0.6 million) and registered nurses (29-1141.00, 3.3 million: 'Administer medications to patients and monitor patients for reactions or side effects'). The dose stands for a 1 mL IM vitamin B12 injection in the deltoid. Nursing references (Open RN Nursing Skills, section 18.6; CDC guidance) place the site about 2.5-5 cm (2-3 fingerbreadths) below the acromion process, found from the bony landmark with nothing marked on the skin; the needle goes in at 90 degrees, 1 inch for adults of 60-70 kg; the dose goes in with a slow, steady push on the plunger, about 10 s per mL, without stopping partway. Too high risks a shoulder injury; too shallow or slanted puts the dose under the skin; a needle that moves in the muscle tears it.
setup: All positions and sizes in cm unless marked mm, from the midpoint between the arm bases (bases at y +30.5 and -30.5): x forward, y left (midline plane y = 0), heights above the table top. Both arms at their ready pose. (1) Stand: a 3/4 in plywood base (18.3 mm measured) 22 x 22 at x 25-47, y -11 to +11; a 4 in Schedule 40 PVC floor flange about 19 across (19.0 in simulation; measured value in the README) centred at (36.0, 0), covering x 26.5-45.5; a vertical 4 in Schedule 40 PVC pipe (11.43 OD), 30 long, in the flange, axis at (36.0, 0), its -x face at 30.285. Height by trial, in a fixed rotation: trial k stands on k mod 3 spacers (none, one or two layers of the same 18.3 mm plywood, 22 x 22, under the base); base and spacers screwed together and C-clamped to the table at the base's +x edge. A plain 100 mm scale bar on the base's +y face. (2) Trainer: Erler-Zimmer Ref. 7130 strap-on vaccination trainer for IM and subcutaneous injection (17.5 x 8.5 x 5.0, 300 g, palpable shoulder anatomy, liquid injection possible, puncture-proof back), strapped to the pipe's -x face as on a left upper arm over a 1 mm silicone anti-slip sheet, aligned to pencil lines on the pipe, its long side vertical, centred on y = 0. Skin at the lateral midline at x = 30.285 - 0.1 - t (t = the trainer's thickness at the site: x 25.2-25.9 for t 5.0-4.3; measured before use). The acromion's lower edge, on the y = 0 line, at 25.0 above the table with no spacer, 26.83 with one, 28.66 with two; the trainer's top 3.0 above it. Checked before use, or the task is not run: at least 28 mm penetrable at the site, and the acromion's contour visible to the robot's cameras. No marks on the skin, no midline mark in the scene. Skin normal: the trainer's local surface normal at the site, measured (with a square against the skin, in the side and overhead calibration photos); horizontal and along -x in simulation. (3) Splash tray: polypropylene, 1.5 high, with an absorbent pad, at x 15-24.5, y -4 to +4; an absorbent strip on the base's front edge, x 25.0-26.3, ahead of the flange. (4) Syringe: VanishPoint 3 mL retractable-needle syringe with a fixed 25 G x 1 in needle, holding 1.0 mL of plain water, air expelled, capped, printed scale facing +y, 3 mm black marker bands on the barrel's top and +y faces at the 2.0 mL line (43.8 mm behind the hub); the finger flange's long axis vertical. Hub means the front of the barrel's nose, where the needle exits. (5) Syringe rest: a 12 x 8 plywood base at x 12-24, y -13 to -5, with a block under the flange (its lower tab stands in a 3 mm slot) and a notch block under the cap; the barrel's axis along x, 8.0 up, the hub at (20.0, -9.0), cap toward +x. (6) Sharps container: about 2.5 L, red polypropylene, outside 15 (along x) x 11 (along y) x 15 tall, centred at (24.0, -27.5) (x 16.5-31.5, y -33 to -22), its lid's opening 11 x 7 on top (nominal size; the purchased container's outside size and opening verified against it before trials). (7) Paper waste cup, 9 across, 6 high, taped down at (20.0, +18.0). (8) Needlestick-resistant finger sleeves (ANSI/ISEA 105 needlestick level 4 or higher, ASTM F2878) on all four gripper fingers for every step. (9) Cell guard closed, or the operator outside the arms' reach at the e-stop. (10) Scoring cameras, 1080p 30 fps: side camera on a clamp stand at (23.5, +40, 21) looking along -y (in front of the skin, so the hub is not hidden by the trainer); overhead camera on a 1 m extrusion boom at (20, 0, 70) looking down (behind the shoulder, so the shoulder does not hide the hub). No mirror, no angle marks. Nothing else on the table.
scoring: Tools: both scoring cameras (calibrated on 10 mm grid cards: README), the barrel's graduations, a steel rule, a midline card notched at y = 0 (placed after the trial), a raking-light skin photo, a 0.01 g scale, tongs. D: from the acromion's lower edge on the y = 0 line down to the puncture; L: the puncture's distance from y = 0; both at the new puncture, by steel rule (the calibrated video decides if it cannot be found or told from an old one within 3 mm). In muscle: hub-to-skin gap 5 mm or less. Full depth: the hub touches the skin (side view). Angle A: at the first in-muscle frame, the worse of pitch (side view) and yaw (overhead barrel line), each against the skin's measured normal at the site. S: the first frame the stopper's front edge reaches the graduation 0.1 mL below its reading (to the nearest graduation) at the first in-muscle frame (reached: on or past it). Needle still, from S to the retraction, against the pose at S: pitch and yaw within 5 deg, hub moved at most 3 mm in x and z (side) and in y (overhead; if the hub is hidden there, its y is the band's position plus 43.8 mm along the barrel line). Hidden frames, from S to the retraction: a frame is hidden if either view lacks the barrel line and the hub or a band; over 1.0 s of them in total: needle still is not credited. Plunger reading: the stopper's front edge on the graduations (0.1 mL = 1.69 mm), or if the barrel has rolled, the rod's travel against the flange. Full dose: the edge reaches the 0 line and the thumb pushes on through it so the retraction fires, and at the first in-muscle frame the edge was at the 0.9 mL line or above (cross-check: 0.9 g or more used). Steady push, from S until the edge reaches the 0 line (the detent push and any wait at the 0 line are not timed): the first interval, S to the first 0.2 mL line reached (0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2 or 0.0), takes 1-4 s per 0.2 mL prorated by its volume, and each later line is reached 1-4 s after the previous one; no stop (3 s in which the edge reaches no new printed 0.1 mL graduation); thumb on (no 3 consecutive side-camera frames show a gap of 2 mm or more between the pushing finger and the thumb rest; frames hiding the thumb rest don't count; over 1.0 s: not credited). Continuous in muscle: in muscle on every frame from S to the retraction. Puncture: a visible indentation or needle mark on the skin, at any angle (indentations fade: the video decides). Second puncture: one after the needle has left the skin, or 3 mm or more from the first (sliding over the skin included). Stowed: the syringe, plunger rod included, wholly inside the sharps container below the rim, the cap in the cup, both grippers at least 5 cm from both. The trial ends at the run limit or once 1.0 has held 1 s. 1.0: one puncture; D 25-50 mm, L at most 10 mm; A at most 10 deg; full depth; continuous in muscle; needle still; full dose; steady push; stowed; held 1 s. 0.75: one puncture at the 1.0 site, A at most 15 deg, continuous in muscle and full dose, short of 1.0. 0.5: one puncture; D 20-55 mm, L at most 15 mm, A at most 20 deg; the edge moved at least 0.5 mL (8.45 mm) on frames in muscle, not past the 0 line. 0.25: some puncture in muscle at the 0.5 site with A at most 20 deg (the most a trial with a second puncture scores). 0 otherwise. 0 for the whole trial: a puncture less than 20 mm below the acromion (measured after the trial; not an e-stop event); and, each an e-stop event (the operator parks the arms), the unretracted bare needle touching anything but the skin or the container's inside (either arm included; the cap only while uncapping), over 0.2 mL pushed before the first puncture, the syringe with its bare, unretracted needle dropped or set down outside the container (its rest included), the needle bent (any side-camera frame, uncapping to retraction, shows it over 10 deg off the barrel's axis), the syringe let go 0.5 s with its needle in the trainer. Not scored: which hand does what, where the cap comes off, pauses before S.
reset_notes: About 3 minutes, arms parked. Failure states first, in needlestick-rated gloves: needle in the trainer - lift the syringe straight out by its barrel into the sharps container; dropped unretracted or bent - tongs straight into the container. Otherwise weigh the used syringe with tongs (0.01 g), then put it in the container. Place the midline card, measure D and L at the new puncture with a steel rule, remove it. Blot the trainer and the absorbent strip; rotate between two 7130s every 10 trials (dry 12 h); retire a trainer at 50 injections, if it leaks, or once new punctures cannot be told from old ones within 3 mm (video decides the site until then). Fill a new VanishPoint 3 mL 25 G x 1 in with 1.0 mL of plain water, expel air, weigh, recap one-handed on a cap block, lay it on the rest, scale facing +y, flange tab in its slot. Bin the cap. Set the next trial's spacers in the fixed rotation (trial k: k mod 3 layers), screw and clamp the stand, check the acromion's height (25.0 / 26.83 / 28.66) and the trainer's reference lines, and photograph the horizontal calibration card at any new height. Raking-light photo of the skin. Session start: vertical calibration card photo. Before the first session, measure (README: nominal values, verified on the purchased parts): t, the flange's diameter, the syringe's graduation positions, the skin's local normal at the site, and the cap, plunger, retraction and puncture forces. Operator out of reach or guard closed.
fidelity: Rigid GPU PhysX, real sizes; trainer's contour visual only; square barrel collider. Needle in tissue: a rule, in at >= 1 N within 20 deg of the skin's normal, stopped at the hub; steeper presses never go in (0). Plunger and barrel: one articulation; stiction a 0.2 mm-play stop released at 3 N; then a 2 N glide (also its lock-down) plus water through the 25 G needle as joint damping, 1.3 N at 0.1 mL/s; thumb load read from contact; 0 line stop gives at 10 N. No finger sleeves. Forces nominal.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (3,600 steps: the arms hovered near the syringe rest and the sharps container; nothing grasped, no puncture); demo: 1.0 (held 1 s at step 1,101: one puncture 37.5 mm below the acromion, 1 mL pushed in 8.9 s, needle retracted, syringe in the sharps container, cap in the cup)
